subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should the shared state DB policy for CLI/status/diagnostic commands be RPC-first with no-maintenance fallbacks, a stricter single-writer gateway lease, or both?
rationale: The source still allows non-gateway processes to open the shared DB through normal WAL-maintained and sometimes write/probe paths, and fixing that crosses CLI UX, doctor migrations, gateway ownership, and recovery policy rather than one isolated call site.

options.title: RPC-first with no-maintenance fallback
options.body: Route health/status/stability through the running gateway whenever possible and make offline fallback opens read-only without WAL/schema/probe/checkpoint side effects while the gateway may be active.

options.title: Single-writer gateway lease
options.body: Make the gateway the only writer and maintenance owner while active, requiring non-gateway processes to refuse, RPC, or enter an explicit offline-maintenance mode.

options.title: Forensics and harness first
options.body: Pause code direction until the reporter's corrupt DB bundle and a native concurrent CLI/gateway harness prove which opener or checkpoint path causes the corruption.

recommendation.title: RPC-first with no-maintenance fallback
recommendation.body: Route health/status/stability through the running gateway whenever possible and make offline fallback opens read-only without WAL/schema/probe/checkpoint side effects while the gateway may be active.

likelyOwner.reason: The broad shared SQLite runtime-state ownership model appears to originate in the DB-first refactor history, making this the best available owner for the boundary decision.
